readings: Using driver standings linked to their races by race id (leaving out standings with no matching race), for each race name (`races.name`) get the average of `driverStandings.points` (ignoring missing values) and the field size, defined as the total number of driverStandings rows for that race name (COUNT of rows, across all its races and years). Then keep the race names whose field size is strictly above the average of this row-count field size across all race names. In one row, give the average of their average points, their average field size, and the average amount by which their field size exceeds the overall average field size. No rounding.

Using driver standings linked to their races by race id (leaving out standings with no matching race), for each race name (`races.name`) get the average of `driverStandings.points` (ignoring missing values) and the field size, defined as the number of distinct drivers (COUNT DISTINCT driverId) appearing in the standings for that race name across all its races and years. Then keep the race names whose distinct-driver field size is strictly above the average of this distinct-driver field size across all race names. In one row, give the average of their average points, their average field size, and the average amount by which their field size exceeds the overall average field size. No rounding.
queries:
WITH per_race AS (
  SELECT r.name AS name,
         AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points,
         COUNT(*) AS field_size
  FROM driverStandings ds
  JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(field_size) AS avg_fs FROM per_race
)
SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points,
       AVG(p.field_size) AS avg_field_size,
       AVG(p.field_size - o.avg_fs) AS avg_excess
FROM per_race p, overall o
WHERE p.field_size > o.avg_fs;
WITH per_race AS (
  SELECT r.name AS name,
         AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points,
         COUNT(DISTINCT ds.driverId) AS field_size
  FROM driverStandings ds
  JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(field_size) AS avg_field FROM per_race
)
SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points,
       AVG(p.field_size) AS avg_field_size,
       AVG(p.field_size - o.avg_field) AS avg_excess
FROM per_race p, overall o
WHERE p.field_size > o.avg_field;
